report.verdict: A clean miss driven by the high end not showing up in either Singapore or Macao: net revenue -3.5% YoY to $3.22bn and adj. property EBITDA -16.7% to $1.12bn, ~13-14% below consensus on a hold-adjusted basis, with group margin -555bps to 34.8% as Macao opex was held flat sequentially into weaker premium spend and MBS mass hold collapsed to 18.7%. Management is doubling down rather than retrenching — $950m of buybacks (19% of the share count retired in 12 quarters), a 20% dividend hike for 2027, and no cuts to the Macao opex base or the $8bn MBS expansion — so the equity case is now a bet on the premium customer returning before leverage and payout optics become a constraint.

summary: **Headline miss on both lines.** Q3-26 net revenue $3,216m (-3.5% YoY, +2.0% QoQ) vs Street ~$3.33-3.35bn; adj. EPS $0.54 vs consensus ~$0.68-0.71 (Zacks $0.71, MarketBeat $0.68); GAAP diluted EPS $0.48 vs $0.61. Consolidated adj. property EBITDA $1,119m (-16.7% YoY, flat QoQ) vs prior-year $1,344m.

**The miss is almost entirely the high end, in both markets.** Management's own framing: premium/VIP patrons visited less frequently in July and September in Singapore and across the premium mass tier in Macao; the quarter was labelled 'aberrational'. No single cause was offered — the World Cup final (19 Jul), general macro uncertainty and (unanswered) questions about Chinese offshore-wealth/tax enforcement were all cited by analysts.

**Which division drove it: MBS.** Marina Bay Sands EBITDA fell $153m YoY (-20.6%) to $590m on revenue -9.9% to $1,294m; Macao EBITDA fell $72m (-12.0%) to $529m despite revenue +1.8% to $1,940m. JPM put MBS hold-adjusted EBITDA ($594m) 13-14% below the bank/consensus range of $680-685m — that is the bulk of the group shortfall.

**Hold was a genuine headwind but not the whole story.** Company-reported rolling-chip hold adjustment was only -$7m to group EBITDA (Macao -$11m, MBS +$4m), so hold-adjusted EBITDA was $1,112m vs $1,299m in Q3-25 (-14.4%). The bigger swing is mass hold, which the company does NOT adjust: MBS non-rolling win 18.7% (vs 24.5% Q3-25, 22.9% Q2-26) and Londoner 18.6% (vs 23.4%). At a 22-23% normalised MBS mass hold, our estimate is ~$95-120m of additional gross win.

**Volumes in Macao were strong — this is a spend-per-head and cost problem, not a traffic problem.** Rolling volume +31% YoY to $5.74bn (our aggregation of property data), non-rolling drop +11% to $7.18bn, slot/ETG handle +26% to $6.60bn; patron count up double digits, property visitation up high single digits; slot/ETG revenue +18% vs a +9% market; retail tenant sales +10%. Mass GGR share 26.1%, the best since Q4-23 — but Macao mass table gross win still fell ~2% YoY on hold.

**Opex is the structural issue in Macao.** Group resort-operations expense +5.3% YoY to $2,103m (65.4% of revenue vs 60.0%) while revenue fell. Macao has added table hours, gaming/sales/hospitality headcount over the past year; management says fixed costs are now flat sequentially and headcount will not rise materially, but explicitly refused to cut — the hires are framed as pre-investment for the renovated product. Macao margin 27.3% (-426bps YoY, +325bps QoQ off a hold-hit Q2).

**MBS non-gaming remains the quality part of the print.** Rooms +5.2%, F&B +9.5%, ADR +5.7% to $1,038, RevPAR +6.1% to $994 at 95.8% occupancy; non-gaming revenue +5.3% YoY to $378m. Casino revenue -14.9% to $916m did the damage. Management reiterated an unchanged $2.7-2.8bn annual EBITDA run-rate for MBS (c.$675-700m/qtr) — Q3 was $590m.

**Macao target reiterated: $700m quarterly EBITDA 'and more over time'.** Q3 was $529m; the 9M-26 run-rate is $531m/qtr. The bridge relies on Venetian renovation completion (CNY 2028; ~400 rooms out in Q3, ~500 through Q4-27; ~600 renovated rooms already back), Conrad-to-Londoner rebrand, and market GGR recovery after what management called several months of contracting market GGR.

**Capital returns stepped up hard into a falling share price.** $950m repurchased (~21m shares at $45.31) vs $787m in Q2 and $5.06bn still authorised under the $6bn July programme; cumulative 145m shares (19.0%) for $6.98bn at $48.03 since Q4-23. Dividend held at $0.30 for Q4-26, raised 20% to $0.36/qtr ($1.44/yr) from Q1-27. A further 62m SCL shares bought for HKD793m (~$101m), lifting ownership to 75.56%.

**Balance sheet absorbing the payout.** Unrestricted cash $2.86bn (from $3.38bn at Q2) and gross debt $15.30bn (from $15.11bn); net debt ~$12.44bn, up ~$0.7bn QoQ. On annualised 9M-26 adj. property EBITDA (~$4.88bn, our estimate) gross leverage is ~3.1x and net ~2.5x, at the top of the stated 2-3x gross target (which excludes development debt). Liquidity: $4.27bn of revolvers plus a $4.57bn delayed-draw term loan ring-fenced for the MBS expansion.

**Cash flow (our estimate, 10-Q not reviewed):** Q3 EBITDA $1,119m less interest ~$186m, cash taxes ~$100m, corporate ~$88m and capex $281m implies ~$460m of pre-minority free cash flow versus ~$1.24bn returned (buybacks $950m, dividend ~$192m, SCL purchases ~$101m) — consistent with the $520m cash decline and $190m debt increase. Buybacks are running at roughly 2x FCF.

**Capex and the MBS expansion.** Q3 capex $281m (Macao $154m, MBS $121m, corporate $6m). The MBS expansion is quantified at $8bn including ~$2bn of land premium, with a ~15,000-seat arena, opening targeted early 2031 subject to approvals; a 'good portion' of construction cost is locked, with fit-out still exposed to inflation. Macao maintenance capex is guided at ~$300m/yr against $750-800m of D&A; 2027 Macao development capex covers the Venetian, the Conrad rebrand and an accelerated botanic-garden concession commitment.

**Tax and below-the-line drag.** Effective tax rate 22.5% (vs 15.6%), driven by the 17% Singapore statutory rate on a larger MBS share of profit and lower Macao contribution; interest income fell to $23m from $39m on lower cash; interest expense flat at $186m with a 4.7% average cost. Net income $352m (-28.3%), attributable $304m (-27.4%). Diluted shares -6.6% YoY to 640m cushioned EPS.
**Sands China (SCL):** GAAP net revenue +1.4% to $1.93bn, net income -29.8% to $191m. SCL minorities absorbed $48m of group net income (vs $72m).

**9M-26 is still ahead on revenue but behind on profit.** Revenue $9,955m (+6.3%), operating income $2,140m (+1.4%), adj. property EBITDA $3,659m (-4.2%), GAAP EPS $1.86 (+5.1%, share-count driven), adj. EPS $2.04 (-5.1%). Macao 9M revenue +8.0% with EBITDA -6.5%; MBS 9M revenue +4.4% with EBITDA -2.3%.

**No formal guidance; sell-side reset.** JPM cut Q4-26 adj. property EBITDA 4% to $1.26bn and 2027/2028 by ~2% to $5.06bn/$5.15bn; BofA (Neutral) cut its PT to $45 from $50, Mizuho (Outperform) to $54 from $61, Barclays (Overweight) to $50, JPM to $54. October was flagged on the call as potentially a fifth consecutive month of YoY Macao market GGR decline (analyst assertion, not company data).

**Strategy and M&A.** Management ruled out M&A ('interested in buying more of our company'), dismissed take-private speculation, and said reinvestment (promo) in Macao is being optimised lower sequentially while gaining share; competitive intensity is unchanged with no escalation seen. NBA Games Week year two in October was described as more successful than 2025, financials to come in January.

**Thesis read-through.** Volume share gains, rising SCL ownership and shrinking share count are real. But the quarter exposes the gearing of the model to a thin cohort of super-premium players in two buildings, into which the company is layering a higher fixed-cost base and an $8bn project. Until the premium customer visibly returns (Q4 seasonality plus Golden Week/NBA week is the first test), the equity is a leverage-tolerant buyback story rather than an earnings-growth story.

segments.name: Macao Operations (Sands China Ltd, 75.56% owned)
segments.headline: Volumes and share up strongly, but hold at the Londoner and a fixed-cost base built for a bigger market pulled EBITDA -12% YoY to $529m; the $700m quarterly target is now a 2028 story.
narrative: They grew Macao net revenue 1.8% YoY (and 8.4% QoQ off a hold-hit Q2) to $1,940m, while adjusted property EBITDA fell 12.0% to $529m and margin compressed 426bps to 27.3% (though +325bps sequentially). Rolling-chip hold ran slightly above the 3.3% expectation, so hold-adjusted EBITDA would have been $11m lower at $518m — versus $599m hold-adjusted in Q3-25. On the Sands China GAAP basis, net revenue rose 1.4% to $1.93bn and net income fell 29.8% to $191m. Casino revenue across the five properties was $1,454m, +1.7% YoY and +10.4% QoQ; non-gaming revenue (ex ferry) was broadly flat at ~$448m.

The volume story is genuinely good and is what management chose to lead with. Rolling volume rose 31% YoY to $5.74bn (our sum of the property disclosures; -24% QoQ as Plaza/Four Seasons VIP play normalised from a $2.8bn Q2), non-rolling drop rose 11% to $7.18bn (flat QoQ) and slot/ETG handle rose 26% to $6.60bn. Mass GGR share reached 26.1%, the strongest since Q4-23, patron count grew double digits and property visitation high single digits, and slot/ETG revenue grew 18% against a market that grew 9% in that segment. Retail tenant sales were +10% YoY despite a weak China consumption backdrop. Yet Macao mass-table gross win (drop × hold, our calculation) was still down ~2% YoY at ~$1.47bn because the Londoner's non-rolling hold fell to 18.6% from 23.4% — management attributed this to playing unlucky against the super-high end of premium mass, which it was able to capture this quarter for the first time in a while. The read is that share gains are being bought at the top of the mass pyramid, where hold volatility is highest and where the customer base thinned in the quarter.

By property, the Londoner was flat on revenue at $685m but EBITDA fell 18.7% to $178m (margin 26.0%, -590bps) despite rolling volume +39% to $3.22bn and non-rolling drop +24% to $2.80bn; a normal ~21-22% mass hold would have added roughly $70-95m of gross win (our estimate). The Venetian, mid-renovation with ~400 rooms out (rising to ~500 through Q4-27), saw revenue -6.2% to $649m and EBITDA -15.3% to $205m (31.6% margin), with table count down to 629 from 657 and slots down to 1,410 from 1,660; management says mass revenue improved sequentially and feedback on the ~600 renovated suites has exceeded expectations, with full reintroduction targeted for Chinese New Year 2028. The Plaza/Four Seasons rebounded sharply from Q2's negative VIP hold: revenue +15.5% YoY to $238m, EBITDA +14.9% to $85m (35.7% margin), RevPAR +6% to $485. The Parisian grew revenue 6% to $231m on slot handle +39% but EBITDA fell 13% to $46m (19.9% margin, -440bps), and Sands Macao grew revenue 37.5% to $99m with EBITDA $14m, helped by slot handle more than doubling to $1.57bn after machine relocations. Hotel metrics were firm everywhere — occupancy 96-99%, Londoner RevPAR $257 (+$4), Venetian $197 flat.

The cost base is the bear point and management did not blink. Over the past year they have added table operating hours, gaming, sales/marketing and hospitality headcount and raised service levels; Grant Chum said this step-up is now embedded in Q2 and Q3, fixed costs are essentially flat sequentially, and headcount will not rise meaningfully beyond cost-of-living inflation next year. Asked directly whether opex should be revisited given softness, Patrick Dumont said the focus is on investing for growth, not cutting the people just hired — the staff are being trained ahead of the renovated product coming online. Reinvestment (promotional) intensity in the market is unchanged, with no escalation seen; Sands says it has been optimising its programme lower sequentially since Q1 while gaining share, and expects industry reinvestment to moderate only when market revenue recovers. Competitors are reportedly starting to fine-tune reinvestment because industry margins are not where they were.

On outlook, the $700m quarterly EBITDA goal was reiterated 'and more over time', but it is contingent on the Venetian refresh (CNY 2028), the Conrad-to-Londoner rebrand and an accelerated botanic-garden concession project, alongside ~$300m/yr of maintenance capex against $750-800m of D&A. Seasonally Q4 should be stronger than Q2/Q3 on October Golden Week — now extended by NBA Games Week year two, which management described as more successful than 2025 across the resort, fan zone and MICE — but the company conceded the market has had several months of contracting GGR and would not forecast how seasonality plays against that. The World Cup drag was sharper in June/July than August/September. We would model Q4-26 Macao EBITDA in a $560-600m range (estimate), still ~$100m+ below target, and treat the 26.1% share print as the metric to track for evidence the opex investment is paying back.

segments.name: Marina Bay Sands (Singapore)
segments.headline: Revenue -9.9% and EBITDA -20.6% to $590m as super-premium visitation fell in July/September and mass hold dropped to 18.7%; non-gaming and volumes held up, and the $2.7-2.8bn run-rate was reiterated.
narrative: They delivered MBS net revenue of $1,294m, down 9.9% YoY and 6.2% QoQ, with adjusted property EBITDA of $590m (-20.6% YoY, -14.4% QoQ) and margin of 45.6%, down 615bps YoY and 433bps sequentially. Rolling-chip hold of 4.53% was marginally below the newly raised 4.6% theoretical, so hold-adjusted EBITDA was $594m — against $700m hold-adjusted in Q3-25 (when 4.84% win was measured against a 4.2% theoretical) and $726m in Q2-26. Note the theoretical rolling hold has been lifted to 4.6% from 4.2%, which flatters the hold-adjusted comparison: measured against the old 4.2% basis, Q3-26 rolling play would have been 'lucky', not unlucky. Casino revenue fell 14.9% to $916m; every non-gaming line grew.

Volumes were not the problem. Rolling volume was $8.43bn, down 7.1% YoY and 9.1% QoQ but still the third-highest quarter in the property's recent history; non-rolling drop rose 12.6% YoY to $2.87bn and slot handle 2.1% to $6.54bn. The damage came from hold on mass: non-rolling win of 18.7% compared with 24.5% in Q3-25 and 22.9% in Q2-26 took mass-table gross win to ~$537m from ~$625m (our drop × hold calculation, -14% YoY) on 13% more drop. Had MBS held at 22-23% on mass, gross win would have been ~$95-120m higher (estimate), which on a ~70-75% flow-through would have put EBITDA close to the $675-700m quarterly run-rate management continues to cite. Rolling gross win fell 13% to ~$382m on lower volume. Slot win was ~$288m, +2%.

Management's explanation was that its highest-value patrons simply visited less in July and September, with the World Cup final, broad macro uncertainty and unspecified sentiment factors all mentioned; the side-bet product introduced over the past two years adds hold volatility in both directions, and the company stressed 'the door swings both ways'. Patrick Dumont was explicit that nothing has changed in the view of MBS as a $2.7-2.8bn annual EBITDA property and that the quarter was aberrational. MBS's catchment is Southeast Asia (Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Korea, Japan) rather than China, so overlap with the Macao premium customer is limited — yet sentiment weakened in both simultaneously, which management could not explain. A fuller Q4 will tell us whether this was timing or a cohort issue in a casino that is, by design, concentrated in a small number of very high-value players.

The non-gaming engine kept running: rooms revenue +5.2% to $162m, F&B +9.5% to $104m, mall +1.4% to $70m and convention/other +2.4% to $42m, for non-gaming revenue of $378m (+5.3% YoY, +6.2% QoQ). ADR rose 5.7% to $1,038 and RevPAR 6.1% to $994 at 95.8% occupancy, underscoring that the 2023-25 suite programme (132 to ~770 suites) continues to price up. The Shoppes at MBS generated $70m of gross revenue at an 88.6% operating margin, 99.5% occupancy and $3,318 tenant sales per sq ft. MBS capex was $121m in the quarter (vs $215m in Q2).

On the expansion, the budget is $8bn including ~$2bn of land premium, with a ~15,000-seat arena intended to be the region's premier live-entertainment and MICE venue, a new tower with a wellness/residential feel aimed at the growing, younger super-premium cohort, and opening targeted for early 2031 subject to approvals. A good portion of construction cost is locked, but fit-out remains exposed to inflation and management is being cautious. Funding runs through a dedicated $4.57bn delayed-draw term loan, which sits outside the 2-3x gross leverage target. Management's argument is that peak-period capacity is already a constraint for its top tier; the counter-argument, which this quarter illustrates, is that the returns on $8bn are highly sensitive to the frequency with which a few hundred customers choose to visit. We model Q4-26 MBS EBITDA in a $640-680m range (estimate) assuming mass hold normalises toward 22-23% and partial return of high-end visitation.

highlights.text: Macao volume and share momentum: rolling volume +31% YoY, non-rolling drop +11%, slot/ETG handle +26%, mass GGR share 26.1% (best since Q4-23), slot/ETG revenue +18% vs +9% market, retail tenant sales +10% — all while management says promotional reinvestment is being optimised lower sequentially.
MBS non-gaming pricing power intact: ADR +5.7% to $1,038, RevPAR +6.1% to $994, rooms +5.2%, F&B +9.5%; mall at 99.5% occupancy and $3,318 psf. The suite programme is still monetising.

Capital return stepped up into weakness: $950m buyback at $45.31 (vs Q2 $787m), $5.06bn authorisation remaining, 19% of shares retired since Q4-23, dividend +20% to $0.36/qtr from Q1-27, SCL stake lifted to 75.56%. Diluted share count -6.6% YoY.

Hold at the Londoner (18.6% mass) and MBS (18.7% mass, 4.53% rolling vs 4.6% theo) was adverse; at normalised mass hold we estimate ~$165-215m of additional gross win across the two properties — the single largest reconciling item vs consensus and reversible.

Macao opex step-up is now in the base: management says fixed costs are flat sequentially and headcount will not rise materially, so operating leverage should return if/when revenue recovers; Macao margin already +325bps QoQ.
Development expense fell to $37m from $72m and loss on disposal to $4m from $68m; D&A -7.6% — below-the-line GAAP comparisons are getting easier.

Plaza/Four Seasons rebounded from negative Q2 VIP hold to $85m EBITDA (35.7% margin) with RevPAR +6%; Sands Macao EBITDA +75% on relocated slot capacity — the portfolio re-orientation to premium and base mass is showing in the tails.

lowlights.text: The super-premium customer stopped showing up in both markets at once, and management cannot say why. MBS rolling volume -7% YoY, Macao spend per visitor down, July and September singled out as weak. Until Q4 proves otherwise, the 'aberrational' label is an assertion, not evidence.

Group margin -555bps to 34.8% and resort opex up 5.3% YoY (65.4% of revenue vs 60.0%) on falling revenue. Management explicitly refused to revisit Macao staffing; the cost base is sized for a $700m/qtr Macao that is currently printing $529m.

MBS theoretical rolling hold quietly raised to 4.6% from 4.2%, converting what would have been a 'lucky' quarter on the old basis into a 'hold-adjusted' tailwind of +$4m. Hold-adjusted comparisons across periods are no longer like-for-like.

Buybacks (~$950m) plus dividends (~$192m) and SCL purchases (~$101m) ran at ~2.7x our estimated pre-minority FCF (~$460m): cash -$520m to $2.86bn, gross debt +$190m to $15.30bn, net debt ~$12.4bn. Gross leverage ~3.1x on annualised 9M EBITDA (est.) is already at the top of the 2-3x target before any MBS development debt.

Macao market GGR has been contracting for several months per management, with October potentially a fifth consecutive down month (analyst assertion on the call); the Venetian carries ~500 rooms out of service through Q4-27, so the $700m target is effectively a 2028 event.

Effective tax rate 22.5% (vs 15.6%) and interest income -$16m YoY as cash is spent — the mix shift toward Singapore (17% statutory) and lower cash balances structurally compress EPS conversion from EBITDA.

$8bn MBS expansion (opening early 2031) is being committed on the thesis that peak-period super-premium capacity is the constraint; this quarter shows demand from that cohort can disappear for two months with no warning, and fit-out costs are not yet locked.

forecast.intro: LVS gives no formal guidance; the 'bridge' is management's reiterated targets versus consensus resets. Nothing was cut: the Macao $700m quarterly EBITDA goal, the MBS $2.7-2.8bn annual run-rate, the $8bn MBS expansion (early-2031 opening) and the Venetian reintroduction by CNY 2028 were all reaffirmed, and the capital-return framework was raised (2027 dividend +20%, $5.06bn buyback capacity). The division that moved the numbers is MBS — JPM put its hold-adjusted EBITDA 13-14% below the $680-685m consensus — with Macao a secondary drag from opex. The sell-side responded by trimming rather than rebasing: JPM cut Q4-26 group adj. property EBITDA 4% to $1.26bn and 2027/28 by ~2% to $5.06bn/$5.15bn; BofA, Mizuho, Barclays and JPM cut price targets to $45-54.

bridge.title: Macao quarterly EBITDA target
bridge.change: Q3 actual $529m; 9M run-rate $531m/qtr; path = Venetian refresh (CNY 2028) + market recovery

bridge.title: Capital return
bridge.change: Q3 buyback $950m (Q2 $787m); gross leverage target 2-3x ex development debt

forecast.view: Our Q4-26 estimate is net revenue of **$3.30-3.40bn** and adj. property EBITDA of **$1.20-1.28bn** (margin ~36-38%), built from Macao **$560-600m** (Golden Week plus NBA Games Week seasonality and a flat fixed-cost base, offset by a contracting market and ~500 Venetian rooms out) and MBS **$640-680m** (mass hold reverting toward 22-23% is worth ~$70-90m of EBITDA on our arithmetic; only partial return of super-premium visitation assumed). That implies FY26 adj. property EBITDA of roughly **$4.85-4.95bn** versus $3.82bn for 9M-25 plus an unverified Q4-25, and Q4-26 adjusted EPS of about **$0.65-0.72** (estimate: EBITDA less ~$345m D&A, ~$85m corporate, ~$165m net interest, ~21% tax, ~$60m minorities, on ~628m diluted shares). The risk to these numbers is skewed down if October's Macao market GGR is indeed a fifth consecutive decline and if MBS high-end visitation did not recover in the Golden Week window. **Margin** should recover sequentially on hold alone but will not regain Q3-25's 40%+ until revenue grows into the Macao cost base. **Leverage direction is up**: with buybacks running ~2x FCF, net debt should climb a further ~$0.5-0.7bn per quarter at the current pace, taking gross leverage above 3x on an LTM basis during 2027 before the $4.57bn MBS delayed-draw term loan is drawn — expect management to lean on the 'ex development debt' definition and the investment-grade rating, and expect the buyback pace to moderate from $950m if EBITDA does not rebound. The structural positives (share gains, non-gaming pricing, shrinking share count, 75.6% SCL ownership) are intact; the structural negative is that earnings are increasingly geared to a few hundred customers' travel decisions, into which the company is adding fixed cost and $8bn of capacity.
watch: Q4-26 Macao: whether Golden Week/NBA Games Week and the 26.1% mass share convert into EBITDA >$560m with opex flat QoQ — and whether DICJ market GGR turns positive YoY after several down months.

MBS mass hold and rolling volume in Q4: mass hold back above 22% and rolling volume >$9bn would validate 'aberrational'; a second quarter of <20% mass hold or rolling <$8.5bn would point to a cohort/behavioural shift.
Capital return vs leverage: buyback pace vs $950m, cash below $2.5bn, gross debt/LTM EBITDA relative to the 3x ceiling, and any rating-agency commentary ahead of MBS DDTL drawdowns.

Venetian renovation cadence: rooms out of service (~500 guided through Q4-27), ADR/RevPAR on renovated inventory, and progress on the Conrad-to-Londoner rebrand and botanic-garden commitment in the 2027 capex plan.
MBS expansion cost discipline: proportion of the $8bn (ex $2bn land premium) locked, fit-out inflation, and timing of government approvals for the early-2031 opening.
Chinese policy/tax developments affecting offshore wealth and premium outbound travel — the question analysts asked three times and management declined to address.
